diagnostics.title: Two lenses on the same conversation
diagnostics.description: Tap through the tabs to see both full diagnostics exactly as the app renders them.

now.title: What’s happening right now
points: Sustained caregiving and work demands sit alongside chronic tension and a composed exterior, creating a quiet loneliness behind her competence.
She’s caught in an inner conflict, craving rest while an inner critic insists she keep producing, triggering guilt and a hyper-responsibility rebound.
Micro-experiments, pausing in the driveway or texting her sister, prove gentle self-care and shared support already soften the load.

items.title: Rest must be earned by crisis
items.body: This rule convinces her she can slow down only when everything breaks. Perfectionism and rumination then keep the system in overdrive.

items.title: Don’t add to anyone else’s load
items.body: The rule silences her needs to protect others, making every help request feel dangerous and increasing the internal pressure to perform.

item.title: The weight of the invisible load
item.body: Caregiving + work + guilt loop through guilt → tension → avoidance of rest → deeper exhaustion. The body stays braced even when nothing is wrong.

item.title: The hidden caretaker cycle
item.body: She manages every role silently, avoids rest because of inner rules, then experiments cautiously with self-care. The cycle maintains the belief that worth equals keeping everything running.

leverage.title: Leverage points
points: The two-minute pause before home interrupts automatic tension and turns rest into an embodied experience instead of a performance.
Asking for help (Thursday dinner) cracks the rule against sharing the load and invites connection.

start.title: Where to start
points: Practice the two-minute pause before entering the house. It’s brief, self-directed, and builds trust in slowing down. Difficulty: gentle.
Send one help request, the Thursday dinner text, to challenge the rule against burdening others. Difficulty: gentle.
Notice one moment of tension, shoulders or throat, and greet it with curiosity. Difficulty: gentle.

resources.title: Resources suggested
points: Self-compassion · Cultivate kindness toward the exhausted inner critic. Beginner.
Mindfulness techniques · Short pauses and body awareness to reduce overwhelm. Beginner.
Anxiety management · Gently challenge anticipatory fear and negative self-talk. Intermediate.

values.secondary: guilt · anxiety about burdening others · ambivalence about rest
values.risk_body: Level: low. No crisis observed; emotional intensity is moderate and congruent. User is engaged and responsive to therapeutic experiments.

items.title: Emotional exhaustion under a composed exterior
points: Carrying family logistics since her mother’s surgery.
Snapping when fatigued, then over-correcting to appear reliable.
Guilt whenever she contemplates rest.

items.title: Chronic physical tension and somatic holding
points: Shoulder and throat tightness, cheek biting, buzzing hands.
Tension eases when micro-rest rituals land.
Body braces for anticipated disappointment.

items.title: Overresponsibility and indispensability beliefs
points: Hidden to-do lists; reluctance to delegate to sister or team.
Core beliefs: If I slow down, everything falls apart and My worth depends on keeping everything running.
Silent rules: rest must be earned; don’t add to anyone else’s load.

items.title: Avoidance behaviors and inner critic resistance to rest
points: Late-night scrolling, productivity loops, ambivalence toward pausing.
Inner critic dismisses rest as dramatic.
Micro-rest experiments show emerging readiness.

distortions.title: Cognitive distortions (5)
items: Should statements · Frequency: 6 · Severity: moderate. Productivity rules define worth.
Personalization · Frequency: 5 · Severity: moderate. Interprets every burden as her responsibility.
Emotional reasoning · Frequency: 5 · Severity: moderate. Reads tension as proof she’s failing.
Mental filter · Frequency: 4 · Severity: moderate. Focuses on risks of rest, overlooks wins.
Catastrophizing · Frequency: 3 · Severity: moderate. Anticipates collapse if she slows down.

therapist_focus.title: Therapist focus
points: Target indispensability beliefs and rest-related guilt.
Pair compassion work with body regulation practices.
Reinforce micro-rest rituals and somatic check-ins.
Challenge should statements and catastrophizing.
Support gradual delegation and shared support experiments.

clinical_interpretations.title: Clinical interpretations
points: Perfectionism plus caretaking burden sustain chronic arousal.
Silent rules maintain avoidance of rest and help.
Distortions amplify guilt and difficulty disengaging.
Behavioral experiments signal readiness for deeper change.

treatment_recommendations.title: Treatment recommendations
points: Cognitive restructuring for should statements and catastrophizing around delegation.
Compassion-focused interventions to soften the critic.
Consistent micro-rest rituals and body awareness techniques.
Guided help-seeking experiments to dismantle overresponsibility.
Monitor emotional intensity and ambivalence toward rest to pace work.

professional_language.title: Professional language
points: Chronic caregiving burden with perfectionism sustains sympathetic activation.
Core schemas of indispensability and conditional self-worth inhibit help-seeking.
Distortions (should statements, personalization, catastrophizing) perpetuate maladaptive coping.
Therapeutic engagement is moderate-high with emerging behavioral activation.
Low acute risk supports CBT and compassion-based approaches.

clinical_insights.title: Clinical insights
points: Mind–body integration is essential given somatic tension.
Rest ambivalence stems from internalized silent rules.
Micro-rest successes show leverage for core belief shifts.
Ongoing monitoring of intensity will guide pacing and intervention depth.
